descriptionChirho: That which is concealed from view or knowledge, used both adjectivally and substantively in the NT. In Matt 6:4-18 Jesus repeatedly contrasts public religious display with acting 'in secret' (ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ), where the Father who sees in secret will reward openly (deu verborgen, fra caché, heb סֵתֶר/נִסְתָּר, hin gupt, kor eunmilhan got). In John 7:4,10 and 18:20 it describes acting secretly versus publicly (spa oculto/secreto). The substantive neuter plural κρυπτά denotes 'hidden things' revealed by God: 1 Cor 4:5 the hidden things of darkness, 1 Cor 14:25 secrets of the heart, 2 Cor 4:2 hidden things of shame (hin guptbātẽ, kor sumgyeojin geotdeul). Rom 2:16 uses it for the secrets God will judge (spa cosas ocultas). Rom 2:29 and 1 Pet 3:4 apply it to the inward, hidden person of the heart. All clusters represent one core sense of concealment with inflectional and number variation (DNS, NNS, NMS, ANP).
